brief: Design an interface for "Memory Altitude" - a personal reflection tool where users map their most vivid memories across a topographical landscape that rises and falls based on emotional intensity, with each memory existing as a translucent geological layer that can be excavated by dragging vertically through time strata, revealing how memories transform and interconnect across years, where the challenge is creating a coherent navigation system that lets users traverse both horizontally across li
critique: While the geological metaphor for memories shows promise, the execution feels incomplete with clunky hover interactions, inconsistent spatial relationships, and a disconnected time scale that adds visual noise without meaningful functionality. The interface lacks the polish and behavioral sophistication needed to elevate the concept beyond a static visualization with basic CSS hover states.
fixes: Simplify the visual hierarchy by removing either the 3D perspective or the complex navigation plane - commit to one spatial metaphor
Replace the crosshair cursor and excavation mechanics with subtle hover states that don't require mode switching
Implement responsive design and complete the truncated CSS to ensure the interface works across devices
